title: Joy in the Ordinary Days
premise: We've reserved happiness for the highlights and written off the ordinary days as filler. But the filler is the life.

title: Who Are You Outside of Work
premise: Your company can separate you from your work overnight. If your work is your whole identity, they can separate you from yourself overnight.

title: Life Moves On (Fresh Deliveries)
premise: "Life moves on" is usually comfort. Read literally it's almost a threat — life doesn't move on from your troubles, it just moves, and today arrives with its own fresh deliveries whether you unpacked yesterday's or not.

title: What's the Worst That Can Happen
premise: "What's the worst that can happen" is never a real question — it's a confidence ritual. And sometimes the worst gets served anyway, plated, on a Versace dish with the Medusa staring back.

title: Things That Should Be Crimes · EP 01: Fake School Fees
premise: Series opener. Some things aren't legally crimes but should be.

title: You Cannot Become What You Don't See
premise: The first person who ever paid me a salary was a woman who owned the place and ran it with drive. I didn't know it was doing anything to me at the time.

title: Trust Your Hands, Not Your Mouth
premise: Words come cheap because they come natural — they cost nothing, so they prove nothing. Action costs something, so only action is evidence.

title: Stop Policing Reading
premise: We are too much of a non-reading people to be policing reading this much. The gatekeeping almost never comes from the big readers — it comes from people performing a relationship with reading rather than doing it.

title: A Dent in the Edge of Everything We Know
premise: I rate people who do PhDs — not for intelligence, for the commitment of time and mental resources to one specific fragment of knowledge. And underneath it, my own quiet realisation: I wanted the title more than I wanted the question.

title: You Were Just the Equipment
premise: When someone has to keep announcing that they're the provider, the protector, the providing isn't the end — it's a means. The real goal is identity, the feeling, the social value.

title: I Am a Freaking Adult Who Cannot Ride a Bike
premise: Decided to learn to cycle in one week, having never ridden in my life. The class turned out to be for experts.

title: 150 Seats, Millions in the Room
premise: In 1991 the World Wide Web went public and access multiplied by billions. Our capacity multiplied by zero.

title: Compliment the Decision, Not the DNA
premise: Rule of thumb for complimenting people, especially strangers: compliment something they chose. Braids, jewellery, perfume, jacket, bag, hair colour.

title: You Might Just Be Comfortable
premise: "People who aren't even doing as much as me are getting ahead" hides an assumption nobody checks: that you know how much they're doing. You don't.

title: One Size Fits All
premise: A spoken-word / psalm-style piece. "One size fits all" is usually the lie on the label — fits nobody.

title: They Handed You a Leash and Called It Armour
premise: "Be capable of violence, just keep it in reserve" fails, because a vice is an appetite, not a tool — and pride is the ingredient that turns a capacity into a disposition. The tell is that these people flip out when it isn't needed.

title: There Is a Man Missing From That Phrase
premise: "Teenage pregnancy" is an agentless phrase — no adult, no man anywhere in it. It names the symptom and hides the disease.

title: They're Cold to You Because They Trust You Not to Leave
premise: The idea that the present parent "teaches" the child to hate the absent one is backwards. Kids idealize the absent parent (a highlight reel) and offload their anger onto the present one (the safe target).

title: A Pet With a Human Face
premise: The (mostly unadmitted) craving for a permanent higher-power position over a partner isn't sustainable — not because hierarchy is evil, but because a human being grows, and you'd have to actively suppress that growth forever to hold the gap. That's not love, it's the textbook definition of abuse.

title: The Art of Not Knowing
premise: We've lost the art of being okay with not knowing. The gap between realizing you don't know something and knowing it used to be long — and curiosity lived in that gap.

title: There's Always More Than the Caption
premise: Humans are nuanced, never black and white — and social media makes us forget it because the format can't hold nuance. The proof is your own body: even the belly button, the most universal "everyone-has-it-the-same-way" thing, has innies, outies, and none.

title: Reserve It for What You Can Reach
premise: After a season of consuming world news all day, her emotions went cold — not because she stopped caring, but because compassion doesn't scale up with numbers, it scales down (psychic numbing). The feed drains the finite feeling that turns into action and leaves nothing for the neighbour at your own junction.

title: Here, and There, and Here Again
premise: Life isn't a line, it's an oscillation — here and there, well then not well, things fall into place then fall out. The wave isn't the malfunction, it's the design.

title: Come Back to Your First Love
premise: A plea, not an argument. Please, open a book today.

title: A River That Never Runs Dry
premise: For the African Christian who travels out: resist the temptation to rank your home faith against the Western one. The gospel isn't tied to any culture — the Christ of Peter is the Christ of Paul.

title: Human Beings Need Other Human Beings
premise: Prolonged isolation is used as punishment because it works, even on the hardest people. We are built to need each other, and you cannot "I don't care" your way out of it.

title: You Cannot "I Don't Care" Your Way Out of It
premise: There's a reason prolonged isolation is used as punishment, even on the hardest people in the hardest prisons. We are social creatures.

title: There Is No Spirit of Jezebel
premise: "The spirit of Jezebel" is a label churches throw at women who are strong-willed or "rough on the edges." It isn't in scripture, it's applied almost only to women, it shuts down the conversation, and the Bible actually honours insistent women. Name the actual thing instead.

title: Chosen by God, Not Known by People
premise: You can be chosen by God and your name can stay unknown to people. Somewhere along the line success got redefined to include being known, so people with real impact on the ten people around them still feel like they're doing nothing with their lives.

title: Two Families in One Courtroom
premise: Caleb Flynn, a former American Idol contestant and music pastor in Tipp City, Ohio, was found guilty of killing his wife Ashley so he could be with the woman he was having an affair with. In a courtroom video, it was just his father and mother standing right behind him, while Ashley's family sat in the same room.

title: My Grandfather Had Clean Pigs
premise: A video about pigs actually being clean brought back a memory of her late grandfather, who raised pigs and proudly showed them to her and her cousins on his seventieth birthday. His pigs were clean.

title: The Binary Mode of Thinking
premise: There's something she calls the binary classification of knowledge, and social media promotes it. Heavy users start thinking in two boxes: good or bad, for or against, success or failure.

title: To Teach Is to Learn
premise: You cannot be a teacher without being a learner, and it isn't a season you graduate from. If you are to keep teaching, you have to keep learning.

title: A Very Slippery Slope With Human Life
premise: The civilised world is treading a very slippery slope with human life. The dignity and value of human life has to keep being emphasised, regardless of the situation.

title: Technology Is Taking More Than It Gives
premise: We need to be much more careful with technology, with how it's built and how much of our lives we hand over to it. This isn't doom-saying.

title: We're Losing the Ability to Hold Context
premise: People say nobody can read anymore, nobody is smart anymore. I don't think that's the whole problem.

title: Should Couples Build an Online Presence Around Their Marriage?
premise: I genuinely don't think it's healthy for couples to build a shared digital presence out of their marriage. I've never been married, so this is from observation, not experience.
